subject.title: Skills: emit a structured event when a skill is excluded for an agent (allowlist/agent-filter blocks are invisible to hooks)

question: Should blocked-skill telemetry represent concrete named requests only, or every skill omitted while preparing an agent’s available-skill snapshot?
rationale: Current architecture prefilters prompt and command exposure and has no unified invocation-denial event, so this choice determines API meaning, event volume, privacy, and implementation ownership.

options.title: Concrete requests only
options.body: Emit when a user or runtime path explicitly names a known skill and resolution rejects it, avoiding passive inventory noise.

options.title: Snapshot exclusion summary
options.body: Emit a per-run summary of all skills omitted by agent filter, allowlist, or requirements during prompt preparation.

options.title: Keep status-only visibility
options.body: Retain CLI, Control UI, and doctor diagnostics without adding a runtime plugin event.

recommendation.title: Concrete requests only
recommendation.body: Emit when a user or runtime path explicitly names a known skill and resolution rejects it, avoiding passive inventory noise.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows direct ownership of adding typed observation hooks and documenting their lifecycle semantics.
